case_title: Amar Singh Yadav v. State of U.P.
aggravating_circumstances: The accused committed the crime in a most cruel and inhuman manner; the victims were helpless wife and young children; the crime was planned and executed meticulously
mitigating_circumstances: There was no reason to believe that the accused cannot be reformed or rehabilitated and that he is likely to continue criminal acts of violence as would constitute a continuing threat to the society
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Sections 302, 307 and 436 IPC and passed death sentence
high_court_outcome: Confirmed the conviction and death sentence
neutral_facts: The accused, a constable, took his wife and four children to a market on the pretext of shopping for his daughter's marriage. Upon returning, he locked the van and set it ablaze, resulting in the death of his wife and two daughters. The prosecution presented evidence including dying declarations of the deceased, eyewitness accounts, and medical reports. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 302, 307, and 436 of the IPC and imposed a death sentence. The High Court upheld the conviction and sentence. The Supreme Court, however, found that the case did not meet the criteria for the 'rarest of the rare' category and commuted the death sentence to life imprisonment with a minimum of 30 years without remission.
